Maria: Quick sync — we need to narrow the operator minimal spec for private deployments so field teams can start validated installs. customers keep asking for deterministic upgrade lanes, customer-managed networking, and a minimal inbound surface.
Sam: Agreed. Can we define a 1.0 minimal that covers ~80% of installs? e.g., single-node operator, kube-proxy compatible, and explicit egress-only control plane.
Jin: +1. Main risk is customers with strict IP-preservation needs. For those we should offer an explicit --preserve-egress-ip toggle.
Alex: Re: upgrade lanes — propose two lanes: "fast" (in-place patch upgrades within a minor) and "safe" (operator-managed canary across tenant slices). Each lane should have clear acceptance gates.
Priya: Launch acceptance criteria draft: (1) successful canary and full upgrade in staging with 0 data loss, (2) <2% error spike on inference in a 24h post-upgrade window, (3) documented rollback steps and verified rollback test.
Maria: Add network-specific checks: BGP/peering handshake test, DNS TTL validation, and a connectivity smoke that validates customer-managed NAT mapping and preserved sockets.
Sam: For operator flags, minimal example: `--preserve-egress-ip=true --control-plane-mode=egress-only --canary-slices=2 --operator-mode=minimal`. Make this the default 1.0 for customers needing static egress.
Jin: KMS/HSM integration must be optional at install time. Air-gapped customers need an offline key bootstrap doc and commands.
Alex: Ops gating question — what SLA should we promise at launch for Private vs Dedicated? Suggest: Private ships without a platform SLA by default, but with an operational playbook, 90-day dedicated launch support, and an explicit support tier for pilot customers.
Priya: Field asks also require upgrade windows that avoid business hours. Expose a schedule API and a CLI flag: `--upgrade-window=\"sun:02:00-04:00\"`. Also expose an API for maintenance scheduling so NetOps can programmatically block windows.
Maria: Agree. Need a minimum API surface for scheduling and the network handshake. Also a one-page NetOps checklist with required ports and an ordered validation flow.
Sam: Draft ports list: inbound 443 (control API), inbound 8443 (handshake/test), internal gRPC 50051, kubelet 10250, outbound 443 to telemetry endpoints (opt-in). Will write a succinct ports+firewall example.
Jin: Canary fallback rules: automatic rollback to previous operator revision if >2% error delta OR latency p50 increase >150ms sustained for 5 minutes. These thresholds will be configurable per-customer. Document in runbook.
Alex: Owners for next steps: Sam — network checklist and ports one-pager; Jin — prototype canary harness and local demo; Priya — runbook template and field acceptance criteria; Maria — product sign-off and customer comms.
Maria: Next milestones: Sam to share ports + one-pager by EOD Tue (1791100000), Jin to provide canary prototype next Wed, Priya to draft runbook and SLA language by Fri. I'll coordinate pilot invites.
Priya: I'll align with Solutions Eng for two pilot customers in the next 6 weeks. Also will gather customer-specific NAT/IP constraints ahead of pilot.
deploy-bot: Reminder created — follow-up sync on operator minimal spec scheduled at 1791013600 (UTC). :bell:
Sam: Small migration note — customers with preexisting NAT mappings might need short rolling restarts to preserve socket affinity; include sample `kubectl rollout restart` snippets and a preflight socket-dump command in the one-pager.
Maria: Good catch. I'll add migration commands and a minimal troubleshooting matrix. Keeping this thread as the live spec tracker. :thumbsup:
